findings: The real Drive Needle constrained decoder builds its allowed tool-name trie from the runtime-provided tool list, so constrained decoding can structurally reject tool names not offered to Needle.

Argument-key constraints in this Drive snapshot expect Needle's direct parameter-map form. Feeding a standard nested OpenAI parameters.properties schema directly causes the constrained key set to contain 'properties' rather than the intended argument names.
The Frank wrapper must therefore flatten/normalize nested tool schemas before Needle constraints, or supply Needle-native direct parameter maps.

The current full-description 51-tool JSON constructed from the Drive registry is 10923 characters; the previously documented 2317-character compact estimate is not representative of this uncompressed serialization. Exact 1024-token encoder fit remains to be measured with the real tokenizer model.

Full model inference was not executed because the accessible Drive repository snapshot contains source/registry but no checkpoint/weights folder or needle.pkl/needle-cq4 artifact. This is a transport/input availability limit, not a sandbox-size limit.
